speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; can you tell me when these symptoms first appeared and if they are painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS).

The recent initiation of captopril and the abrupt discontinuation of meloxicam (which can cause a rebound hypersensitivity reaction) in the context of mucosal ulcers and skin blisters strongly suggests an adverse drug reaction. The hiking history is likely a distractor, and the family history of autoimmune conditions is less specific than the temporal relationship with the medications. Given the severity implied by mucosal involvement, I recommend an immediate workup to confirm the extent of the reaction.

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP), and Urinalysis.
REQUEST IMAGES: Photograph of forearm blisters and oral mucosal ulcers.
